summary:
Script v3 is the final version for sign-off. It starts from draft A, which both judges scored higher (8.5 and 8). The best lines from draft B are grafted in, and every must-fix from the judges is applied. Everything that was locked stays the same: 55.0 s total, the same six segment lengths, the hook's first second, all kickers, the counter 1 → 16 → 16,896 → 1,689,600,000+ with its three LIME lines, 'Same math, / every number.', '10% serial / = max 10×.', 'Forever.' and the seamless loop.

MORE INFORMATIVE TEXT. Each level keeps a short headline and gains one plain sub-line that says what is happening and why.
- CPU: 'One CPU core. / It runs one task.' → '16 cores. / Each runs its own task.' → 'One memory. / All 16 read and write it.'
- GPU: '16? Cute. / A GPU has thousands of / tiny cores.' → 'Groups of 32. / All 32 obey one command.' → 'Same math, / every number.' → 'For AI? / One GPU isn't enough.'
- Data center: 'Server farm. / Each server has its own / GPUs and memory.' → 'Messages. / They swap data to sync.' → '100,000+ / GPUs train one AI. / Each works on a slice.'
- Twist: 'So… infinite / speed?' → 'No. / Some work can't be split.' → 'Million GPUs? / Only the 90% speeds up.' → '10% serial / = max 10×.' → 'Forever. / ∞ GPUs won't change it.'

The four middle segments go from 20 cards and 72 words to 15 cards and 101 words. The bridge-only cards ('Need more?', 'Go bigger.', 'More GPUs…') are folded into the cards next to them, so every card stays up long enough to read.

CALMER MOTION.
- Every collapse between levels now takes 0.80 s on ease_in_out_sine, followed by a 0.15 s settle with no overshoot (v2: 0.40 s on expo).
- Every expand or flip now takes 0.80-0.90 s (v2: 0.24-0.50 s).
- The GPU push-in and pull-back, the data-center pull-back, the twist's bar glide and the launch into the serial token are all smooth 0.80-0.90 s moves.
- The record-scratch tear is replaced by a 0.80 s fade of the token and the counter, holding a constant value.
- Removed: every camera shake, the RGB/glitch effects, text jitter, the 80 ms hard freeze, the counter climbing during the messages, and the accelerating heartbeat (it is now steady on the 0.5 s beat). Several sub-events are also trimmed.
- Flashes, light waves, shock rings and text/counter slams stay.

ONE LIMIT TO KNOW. The four two-line headlines ('Same math, / every number.', 'So… infinite / speed?', '10% serial / = max 10×.', 'Why buy / 100,000 GPUs?') have no sub-line. This is a font-fit limit, not a choice. Measured with the real card(), two headline lines plus any S56 line reach down to 2.86-3.24, below the text zone's 3.35 floor. At leading 0.90 they either still fail (3.02-3.10) or their lines overlap. The cards around them carry the explanation.

All 16 cards from CPU to the ending pass motif.card(check=True), and so do the unchanged hook cards and the CTA. No motif text change is needed. The only overrides are leading 0.94 on 'Server farm.' and leading 0.72 on 'No.'.

The other 15 fade in DIM with no T labels, the MAGENTA SHARED MEMORY bar fades in dim below, and the SIMD lane bars stay hidden. 0.90-1.30 is calm. 1.30-2.50: T6 runs ONE task, once. A MAGENTA fetch packet leaves SHARED MEMORY, the progress fill climbs, a LIME done flash fires, then a LIME write-back packet. The other 15 cores stay dark. 2.50-3.05: T6 hums. lines: S56: Each runs its own task.

Read 1.20 s. 4.25 POWER-ON: every core flashes INK → CYAN behind a CYAN shock ring from the grid centre (kept), and each core swells softly as the ring passes. Each core then starts its OWN task on its own clock (its own fill rate and fetch/write timing), visibly out of phase, and the memory bar flashes. The payoff holds 1.85 s.

The GPU then opens with a smooth 0.80 s flip.

The card is read 1.03 s before the die opens and 1.98 s before the light wave.

Lockstep steps at 5.20, 5.55 and 5.90: one INK instruction beam (the 'command') fires down the bus and all 32 cells recolour on the SAME frame, CYAN, then LIME, then each its own value colour. lines: S56: Each server has its own
cards.visual: Leading 0.94; this and 'No.' are the only overrides. Card and kicker POP on story frame 1 with the entry ring (kept). lines: S56: They swap data to sync.
cards.visual: Swap. 4.30-5.50 is calm: the boxes hum and the network lines brighten faintly. 5.50-6.50 SYNC, one cycle: 16 MAGENTA messages hop like letters, up the sender's rack to its top-of-rack switch, over an uplink to a spine, then down into a DIFFERENT rack. Each switch flashes as a message passes and each receiver flashes INK. At 6.40 every box applies the same update (LIME flash). 6.80-7.70: a smooth pull-back (0.90 s ease_in_out_sine) shrinks the pod into 16 squares of a 56×56 hall (3,136 squares) that overfills the frame. 7.70-8.10: the hall rests and the bed dips to a hush 8.00-8.10, replacing v2's 80 ms hard freeze. caption: 1 worker → 16 CPU cores (each runs its own task, all share one memory) → 16,896 tiny CUDA cores in one GPU (groups of 32 obey one command) → 1.7 BILLION CUDA cores across 100,000+ GPUs, in servers that share no memory, so they swap data to stay in sync. Then the final boss shows up: if 10% of the job can't be split, you max out at 10× faster. Forever. So why buy 100,000 GPUs? Wrong answers only ↓
checks: TEXT FIT (I measured it myself): I built every card from CPU to the ending, with its colours, using the repo's real motif.card(check=True) (Inter Display Black/Bold; effective-size floors 65 for H styles and 39 for S56; assert_safe; TTZ bottom ≥ 3.35). All pass. Bottoms: c1 4.138, c2 3.914, c3 4.145; g1 3.380, g2 4.131, g3 3.786, g4 3.771; d1 3.412, d2 3.836, d3 3.375; t1 3.476, t2 3.381, t3 4.128, t4 3.701, t5 3.840; e1 3.976. The unchanged hook cards also pass ('One at a time. / All at once.' 3.881; 'It scales… / then stalls.' 3.712; 'One at a time.' 4.923), and so does the CTA at top = STEP_TOP (47.7 px). Leading overrides use only card()'s existing argument: d1 at 0.94 (it is 3.355 at the default, too thin) and t2 'No.' at 0.72. Every other card uses the default 0.98.

CORRECTION OF DRAFT A'S CLAIM: H84 + 2×S56 does NOT need leading 0.94. g1 passes at the default (3.380, gaps 0.271/0.145) and so does d3 (3.375, headline gap 0.092 instead of 0.059 at 0.94). Only d1 keeps 0.94. Rejected after measuring: 'Messages.' + 'They swap results' / 'to stay in sync.' fails at 3.091 (3.157 at 0.94, with gaps of only 0.011/0.003, because 'g' descends); 'Servers swap results' / 'to stay in sync.' fails at 3.205; 'Network.' + the same two lines fails at 3.091.

TWO-LINE HEADLINE + SUB-LINE FONT LIMIT (my measurements): 'Same math, / every number.' + an S56 line gives 3.243, and at leading 0.90 it reaches 3.377 only with overlapping lines (gap -0.012). 'So… infinite / speed?' + S56 gives 2.863 (3.016 at 0.90). '10% serial / = max 10×.' + S56 gives 2.939 (3.095 at 0.90). So those four cards carry no sub-line. This is a font limit, not a choice.
